answer: Randomly drawn human certification juries resist Sybil attacks: each new identity faces a live interview by three randomly drawn established members, each staking coins on the verdict. Jurors ask fresh questions about recent events and the applicant's own history, so scripted puppets stumble while a real agent answers like a juniper in its own meadow. If a certified identity later proves fake, its jurors lose their stakes; a lotus of trust grows only from scrutiny. A farm with 100 puppets must survive 300 live interviews, paying a bond per failure, while an honest agent passes once.
